In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Yunus

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for those who disbelieve there will be a drink of scalding water﴾, and so on.

In this noble verse He mentions that those who disbelieve will be punished on the Day of Resurrection by drinking scalding water (ḥamīm) and by a painful punishment. Ḥamīm means boiling water. He describes this ḥamīm in other verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, intensely hot﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 44].

• His saying: ﴿And they will be given boiling water to drink, which will cut their intestines apart﴾ [Muḥammad: 15].

• His saying: ﴿Boiling water will be poured over their heads. By it, what is in their bellies and their skins will be melted﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 19–20].

• His saying: ﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal, which scalds the faces﴾, and so on [al-Kahf: 29].

• His saying: ﴿Then you will drink upon it from scalding water, drinking like thirsty camels﴾ [al-Wāqiʿah: 54–55].

In another place He mentions that the water they are given to drink is ṣadīd (pus, a foul discharge). May Allah protect us and our Muslim brothers from that by His grace and mercy. This is in His saying: ﴿Behind him is Hell, and he will be given pus-water to drink. He will gulp it down and will hardly be able to swallow it﴾, and so on [Ibrāhīm: 16].

In yet another place He mentions that they will be given ghassāq (a cold, foul fluid) to drink along with the scalding water, as in His saying: ﴿This is so; let them taste it: scalding water and ghassāq﴾ ﴿and other punishments of similar kind, in pairs﴾ [Ṣād: 57–58], and His saying: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except scalding water and ghassāq﴾ [al-Naba': 24–25]. Ghassāq is the pus of the people of the Fire, may Allah protect us and the Muslims from it. Its root is from "ghasaqat al-ʿayn," meaning the eye poured forth its tears. It has also been said that linguistically it means something cold and foul-smelling. Scalding water that has reached the utmost of heat is called ḥamīm āN (intensely hot water). Al-muhl is the dregs of oil, or metal melted from copper, lead, and the like. The verses that explain the various kinds of punishment of the people of the Fire are very numerous indeed.

**The words of the Exalted: ﴿And their greeting therein will be, "Peace."﴾**

In this verse the Exalted states that the greeting of the people of Paradise in Paradise is "Peace" (salam). That is, some of them greet others with it, they greet the angels with it, and the angels greet them with it. The Exalted has explained this in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, "Peace."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 44]

• His saying: ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], "Peace be upon you."﴾ [al-Ra'd: 23-24]

• His saying: ﴿They will not hear therein any ill speech, only "Peace."﴾ [Maryam: 62]

• His saying: ﴿They will not hear therein any ill speech or sin, but only the saying, "Peace, peace."﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 25-26]

• His saying: ﴿"Peace," a word from a Lord Most Merciful.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58]

and other verses besides these.

The meaning of salam is the supplication for safety from calamities.

And tahiyyah (greeting) is a verbal noun from "hayyaka Allah," meaning "may Allah lengthen your life."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing. But when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as though he had never called upon Us to a harm that touched him.﴾

In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, mentions that man, in a time of distress, supplicates to his Lord in all his states. Then, when Allah relieves his distress, he turns away from the remembrance of his Lord and forgets what he was in, as though he had never been in it at all.

He clarified this in other places:

• such as His saying: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance; then when He bestows upon him a favor from Him, he forgets what he had been calling upon Him for before﴾ [az-Zumar: 8], and the verse continues;

• and His saying: ﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I was only given it because of knowledge"﴾ [az-Zumar: 49], and the verse continues;

• and His saying: ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself, and when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication﴾ [Fussilat: 51].

The verses on this matter are many.

However, Allah excepted from these blameworthy characteristics His believing servants, by His saying in Surah Hud: ﴿And if We let him taste favor after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "Gone are the evils from me," indeed he is exultant and boastful. Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and great reward﴾ [Hud: 10-11]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer! Allah does not decree for him any decree except that it is good for him. If adversity afflicts him and he is patient, it is good for him; and if ease afflicts him and he gives thanks, it is good for him. And this is not so for anyone except the believer."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: It is not for me to alter it of my own accord.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet ﷺ to say that it is not for him to alter any part of the Qur'an of his own accord. From His saying ﴿of my own accord﴾ it is understood that Allah the Exalted alters from it whatever He wills, with whatever He wills.

He stated this understanding explicitly in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And when We substitute one verse in place of another, and Allah knows best what He sends down...﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Nahl: 101],

• and His saying: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it...﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 106],

• and His saying: ﴿We will make you recite, so you will not forget, except what Allah wills. Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden﴾ [al-A'la: 6, 7].

(p-153) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So I have already lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not reason?﴾

In this noble verse there is a clear proof against the disbelievers of Makkah, because the Prophet ﷺ was not sent to them as a messenger until he had lived among them for a span of time, and that span is forty years. They knew his truthfulness, his trustworthiness, and his justice, and that he was far, utterly far, from lying against Allah, the Exalted. In the Jahiliyyah they used to call him "al-Amin" (the Trustworthy). Allah silenced them with this proof in another place, where He says: ﴿Or did they not recognize their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 69]. For this reason, when Heraclius (Hiraql), the king of the Romans, questioned Abu Sufyan and those with him about the Prophet's ﷺ attributes, Heraclius said to Abu Sufyan: "Did you ever accuse him of lying before he said what he said?" Abu Sufyan said: "I said, 'No.'" Abu Sufyan at that time was the leader of the disbelievers and the chief of the polytheists, yet despite that he acknowledged the truth, and the truth is what even enemies bear witness to.

Then Heraclius said to him: "I know that he would not abandon lying to people only to then go and lie against Allah." End of quotation.

And for this reason Allah rebuked them by His saying here: ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ [Yunus: 16].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Yunus

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah."﴾ and so on.

This noble verse indicates that they hope for the intercession of their idols on the Day of Resurrection. However, other verses indicate that they deny the very principle of the Day of Resurrection,

- such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And we will not be resurrected﴾ [al-An'am: 29],
- and His saying: ﴿And we will not be gathered﴾ [al-Dukhan: 35],
- and His saying: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78],

along with other verses.

The answer is that they hope for their intercession in this world, for the betterment of their livelihood, and in the Hereafter on the assumption that it exists, because they are in doubt about it. Ibn Kathir stated this explicitly in Surah "al-An'am," in his commentary on His saying: ﴿And we do not see with you your intercessors﴾ [al-An'am: 94], and so on. The following supports it: His saying, exalted is He, concerning the disbelievers: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, surely I will have with Him the best [reward]﴾ [Fussilat: 50], and His saying: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾ [al-Kahf: 36]. This is because the conditional particle "in" (إنْ, if) indicates doubt regarding the occurrence of the condition. It is also supported by His saying: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will be established﴾ [al-Kahf: 36], in the two mentioned verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the example of the worldly life is like rain which We send down from the sky﴾ up to His saying: ﴿for a people who give thought﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, has given the example of this world as vegetation, lush and intermingled, one part with another, which soon dries up and becomes dry stubble, as though it had never existed at all. He also gave it the example mentioned in "al-Kahf" in His saying: ﴿And present to them the example of the worldly life: it is like rain which We send down from the sky﴾ [al-Kahf: 45], up to His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Capable of everything﴾. He alluded to this example in "az-Zumar" with His saying: ﴿Then it dries up, and you see it turning yellow; then He makes it crumbled debris. Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding﴾ [21], and in "al-Hadid" with His saying: ﴿Like a rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers, then it dries up and you see it turning yellow, then it becomes debris﴾ [20], and so on.

Note (tanbih)

The comparison in the mentioned verses is, according to the rhetoricians (al-balaghiyyun), a compound comparison (at-tashbih al-murakkab), because the aspect of resemblance (wajh ash-shabah) is an image abstracted from several things: namely, that each of the compared and the compared-to remains for as long as Allah wills, in a state of freshness and perfection, and then soon decays and vanishes. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And [mention] the Day We will gather them all together﴾ — the verse.

In this noble verse He mentions that on the Day of Resurrection He will gather all of mankind together, and verses similar to this are many.

(p-154) And he states explicitly in "al-Kahf" that He will leave none of them behind, by His saying: ﴿And We gathered them, and We left out none of them﴾ [18:47].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 31:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth, or who owns hearing and sight, and who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living? And who arranges the matter?" They will say, "Allah." So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So say, "Will you not then fear [Allah]?"﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that the disbelievers acknowledge that He, majestic and exalted, is their Lord, the Provider, the Manager of affairs, the One who disposes of His dominion as He wills. This is an explicit acknowledgment of His lordship (rububiyyah), and yet they associated others with Him, majestic and exalted is He.

The verses indicating that the polytheists acknowledge His lordship, majestic and exalted is He, and that this did not benefit them because they associated with Him others in His rights, majestic and exalted is He, are many, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 87]

• His saying: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "They were created by the Exalted in Might, the All-Knowing."﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 9]

• His saying: ﴿Say, "To whom belong the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?" They will say, "To Allah."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 84-85] up to His saying: ﴿Then how are they deluded?﴾, and other verses besides these. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except that they are associators [of others with Him].﴾ [Yusuf: 106]

The aforementioned verses are explicit that acknowledgment of His lordship, majestic and exalted is He, does not suffice for entry into the religion of Islam unless one realizes the meaning of "There is no deity except Allah" (la ilaha illa Allah) by negation and affirmation. We have clarified this in surah al-Fatihah (p. 155) in the discussion of His saying: ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [Al-Fatihah: 5].

As for the feigned ignorance of Pharaoh, may Allah curse him, regarding the lordship of Allah, majestic and exalted is He, in his saying: ﴿Pharaoh said, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?"﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 23], it is the feigned ignorance of one who knows, because he was a servant who is managed (marbub), as indicated by His saying: ﴿[Moses] said, "You have certainly known that these [signs] were not sent down except by the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidences"﴾ up to the verse [Al-Isra: 102], and His saying: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls acknowledged them, out of injustice and arrogance﴾ [An-Naml: 14].

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it?"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾.

In these verses Allah silenced the polytheists with an incontrovertible proof (ḥajar), showing that the partners they worship besides Him have no power to do anything, and that He alone, Mighty and Exalted, is the One who originates creation and then restores it to life a second time, and that He guides whom He wills.

He stated the same thing in many other verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Allah is He who created you, then provided for you, then causes you to die, then gives you life. Is there any of your partners who does anything of that? Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Rum: 40].

• And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They have taken besides Him gods who create nothing, while they are created, and who possess no harm or benefit for themselves, and possess no death or life or resurrection﴾ [al-Furqan: 3].

• And His saying: ﴿O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?﴾ [Fatir: 3], and the rest of the verse.

• And His saying: ﴿Is one who creates like one who does not create?﴾ [al-Nahl: 17], and the rest of the verse.

• And His saying: ﴿Or have they made for Allah partners who created like His creation?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 16].

• And His saying: ﴿Say, "Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended for me some adversity, could they remove His adversity?"﴾ [al-Zumar: 38], and the rest of the verse.

• And His saying: ﴿Or who is it that could provide for you if He withheld His provision?﴾ [al-Mulk: 21], and the rest of the verse.

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision; so seek provision from Allah﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 17], and the rest of the verse.

Verses of this kind are many. It is well known that equating what cannot harm, cannot benefit, and cannot control anything with the One in whose hand is all good, who disposes of everything as He wills, is not something that comes from anyone except one who lacks intellect. This is as Allah said, Exalted, concerning the people of that (error): ﴿And they will say, "If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze"﴾ [al-Mulk: 10].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 37:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿This Qur'an could not have been fabricated apart from Allah, but it is a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of the Book, wherein there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds.﴾

In this noble verse, Exalted is He, declared explicitly that this Qur'an cannot be fabricated apart from Allah, that is, falsely attributed to Him, and that there is no doubt that it is from the Lord of the worlds, Majestic and Exalted is He. (p-156) He also indicated that its confirmation of the heavenly Books revealed before it, and its detailing of the beliefs, the lawful, the unlawful, and similar matters, which are undoubtedly from Allah, Majestic and Exalted is He, is evidence that it is not fabricated, and that there is no doubt about its being from the Lord of the worlds. He explained this in other places,

• such as His saying: ﴿There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. It was not a narration invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.﴾ [Yusuf: 111],

• and His saying: ﴿And the devils did not bring it down. It is not befitting for them, nor are they able to do so.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 210, 211],

• and His saying: ﴿And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended.﴾ [al-Isra': 105],

and the verses of this kind are many.

Then, when He, Exalted is He, declared here that this Qur'an could not be fabricated against Allah, He established the decisive proof that it is from Allah. He challenged all creation to produce a single surah like it, and there is no doubt that if it were of the same kind as the speech of created beings, the creatures would have been able to produce its like. When they all failed to do so, certain knowledge and necessary certainty were attained that it is from Allah, Majestic and Exalted is He. He, Majestic and Exalted is He, said in this surah: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful."﴾ [Yunus: 38]. He also challenged them in the surah of "al-Baqarah" with a single surah of its like, by His saying: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah of its like﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 23]. He challenged them in "Hud" with ten surahs like it, by His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated"﴾ up to the end of the verse [Hud: 13]. He challenged them in "al-Tur" with the whole of it, by His saying: ﴿Then let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful﴾ [al-Tur: 34]. In the surah of "Bani Isra'il" He declared the inability of all creation to produce its like, by His saying: ﴿Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if some of them were to others assistants."﴾ [al-Isra': 88], as we have previously mentioned, and He explained that they would not produce its like, also by His saying: ﴿But if you do not, and you will never do it﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 24].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 39:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, they denied that which they did not encompass in knowledge, and its interpretation (ta'wil) had not yet come to them.﴾

The verified view is that its interpretation (ta'wil) here is the actual reality to which the matter will return on the Day of Resurrection, as we have already mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al 'Imran. What confirms the correctness of this is His saying in Surat Al-A'raf: ﴿Do they await anything but its interpretation? On the day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth. So do we have any intercessors?"﴾ [7:53].

The parallel of the verse is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, they are in doubt about My reminder. Nay, they have not yet tasted My punishment.﴾ [38:8].

(p-157) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they deny you, say: "For me is my work, and for you is your work. You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet ﷺ to declare his disavowal of the abhorrent deeds of the disbelievers, denouncing them and making clear the obligation to keep away from them. He explained this meaning in His saying: ﴿Say: "O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshippers of what I worship... and for you is your religion, and for me is my religion."﴾ [al-Kafirun: 1-6]. A similar case is the saying of Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil) and those who followed him to his people: ﴿Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4], and so on.

Allah, may He be exalted, also explained in another place that among the benefits of withdrawing from the disbelievers and the idols, and disavowing them, is that Allah graciously bestows upon one righteous and virtuous offspring. This is His saying in Surat Maryam: ﴿So when he had withdrawn from them and from what they worshipped besides Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob﴾ [Maryam: 49], up to His saying: ﴿...and high station﴾ [Maryam: 50].

Ibn Zayd and others said that the verse ﴿And if they deny you, say: "For me is my work"﴾ [Yunus: 41] has been abrogated by the verses of the sword.

The apparent view is that its meaning is muhkam (definitive, not abrogated), because disavowal before Allah from evil deeds is unquestionably a legislated obligation that remains in force.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 45:

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And the Day He gathers them, [it will be] as if they had not remained but an hour of the day.﴾ The verse.

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted explains that when the disbelievers are gathered, they will consider the period they spent in the abode of this world to be so brief that it seems to them no more than an hour. He explains this meaning in other places, such as His saying at the end of al-Ahqaf (surah 46): ﴿As if they had not remained but an hour of a day, [on the Day] they see what they were promised﴾ [46:35]; His saying at the end of al-Nazi'at (surah 79): ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [79:46], the verse; and His saying at the end of al-Rum (surah 30): ﴿And on the Day the Hour comes, the criminals will swear that they had remained not but an hour﴾ [30:55], the verse.

We have clarified, in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book), the way of reconciling these verses, which indicate that the world seems to them like an hour, with the verses which indicate that it seems to them more than that, such as His saying: ﴿They will whisper among themselves, "You remained not but ten"﴾ [20:103]; and His saying: ﴿They will say, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count"﴾ [23:113]. Refer to it in the commentary on His saying "﴿They will say, 'We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count'﴾" in surah "﴿Certainly will the believers have succeeded﴾" [23:1].

* *

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿They will recognize one another among themselves.﴾

In this noble verse He states that the people of the gathering will recognize one another, so that fathers recognize their sons and sons recognize their fathers, and so on. However, He explains in other places that this mutual recognition will have no effect, so that none of them will ask another anything. As He says: ﴿And no intimate friend will ask about an intimate friend, though they will be made to see them﴾ [70:10-11]; and His saying: ﴿So when the Horn is blown, there will be no relationships among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another﴾ [23:101].

We have also clarified, in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab", the way of reconciling His saying: ﴿So there will be no relationships among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another﴾ with His saying: ﴿And they will turn to one another, questioning each other﴾ [37:27], in the surah "﴿Certainly will the believers have succeeded﴾" as well.

* *

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah, and they were not guided.﴾

In this noble verse He explicitly states the loss of those who deny meeting Him, and that they were not guided. He did not mention here the object of His saying "lost" (khasira). In many places He mentioned causes of loss, and in other places He mentioned the omitted object here. Among the verses similar to this verse is His saying in al-An'am (surah 6): ﴿Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah, until when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they say, "Oh, how we regret what we neglected concerning it"﴾ [6:31], the verse. His saying in al-Baqarah (surah 2): ﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification and sever what Allah has ordered to be joined and cause corruption on the earth - it is those who are the losers﴾ [2:27]. His saying also in al-Baqarah: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recite it as it should be recited; it is those who believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it - it is those who are the losers﴾ [2:121]. His saying in al-A'raf (surah 7): ﴿Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? None feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people﴾ [7:121]. His saying also in al-A'raf: ﴿Whom Allah guides is the one guided, and whom He sends astray - it is those who are the losers﴾ [7:178]. And His saying in al-Zumar (surah 39): ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah - it is those who are the losers﴾ [39:63].

The verses of this kind are many. He, the Exalted, has sworn that no human being will be saved from this loss except through four matters:

First: faith.

Second: righteous deeds.

Third: mutual enjoining of the truth.

Fourth: mutual enjoining of patience.

This is stated in His saying: ﴿By time. Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [103:1-2].

He explains in other places that the omitted object upon which the loss falls is themselves, as in His saying in al-A'raf: ﴿And those whose scales are light - those are the ones who have lost themselves because they had been wronging through Our signs﴾ [7:9]; His saying in al-Mu'minun (surah 23): ﴿And those whose scales are light - those are the ones who have lost themselves; in Hell they will abide eternally﴾ [23:103]; and His saying in Hud (surah 11): ﴿Those are the ones who have lost themselves, and what they used to invent has departed from them﴾ [11:45].

In other places He adds the loss of their families along with themselves, as in His saying in al-Zumar: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss"﴾ [39:15]; and His saying in al-Shura (surah 42): ﴿And those who believed will say, "Indeed, the losers are those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment"﴾ [42:45].

He explains in another place that the loss of the losers may encompass both this world and the Hereafter, which is His saying: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge; if good befalls him, he is reassured by it, but if trial strikes him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss﴾ [22:11].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We cause you to die, to Us is their return﴾ – the verse.

In this noble verse, Allah, may He be exalted, makes clear to His Prophet ﷺ that He may either show him in his lifetime some of the punishment and retribution that He promises the disbelievers, or cause him to die before that. Their return is to Him, may He be exalted and glorified, and nothing escapes Him of what He wills to do to them, because of the completeness of His power over them and the effectiveness of His will concerning them, may He be exalted and glorified. He has also made this meaning clear in other places, such as His saying in Surat "al-Mu'min" (Surah al-Ghafir): ﴿So whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We cause you to die, to Us they will be returned﴾ [40:77], and His saying in "az-Zukhruf": ﴿So whether We take you away, indeed We will take retribution upon them. Or We show you that which We have promised them, and indeed We are Able over them﴾ [43:41–42], and other verses besides these.

Admonition (tanbih)

The Mighty Qur'an has not used the present-tense verb after the conditional "in" (in), which is assimilated into "ma" (ma) added for emphasis of the condition, except when it is joined with the heavy emphatic nun (nun al-tawkid al-thaqilah), such as His saying here: ﴿And whether We show you﴾ – the verse [10:46], ﴿So whether We take you away﴾ – the verse [43:41], ﴿So if you encounter them﴾ – the verse [8:57], and ﴿And if you fear from a people﴾ – the verse [8:58].

For this reason, some grammarians of Arabic claimed that the present verb must necessarily be joined with the aforementioned nun in this situation (p-160), but the truth is that its not being joined with it is permissible, as in the saying of the poet (metre: al-Mutaqarib):

"Fa-immā tarayinnī wa-lī lammatun / fa-inna l-ḥawādith awdā bihā"
(So if you see me, and I have a forelock, indeed the calamities have destroyed it.)

And the saying of another (metre: al-Kamil):

"Za'imat Tumāḍir annanī immā amut / yusaddidu ubaynūhā l-aṣāghir khallatī"
(Tumadir claimed that if I die, the little ones of her sons will take charge of my friendship.)

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 47:**

Allah's words: ﴿And for every nation there is a messenger﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah states explicitly that every nation has a messenger. He clarifies this in other places, such as:

• His words: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger﴾ (al-Nahl: 36),

• His words: ﴿And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them﴾ (Fatir: 24),

• His words: ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾ (al-Ra'd: 7),

along with other verses. The Prophet (ﷺ) also explained that the number of nations is seventy nations, in the hadith of Mu'awiya ibn Haydah al-Qushayri (may Allah be pleased with him): "You are completing seventy nations, you are the best of them and the most honored before Allah." We have clarified these verses in our book *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book), and the way of reconciling them with His words: ﴿so that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned﴾ (al-Ra'd: 6), in the commentary on His words in surah al-Ra'd: ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾.

* *

Allah's words: ﴿So when their messenger comes, judgment is passed between them with justice, and they are not wronged﴾.

Allah clarified the meaning of this noble verse in surah al-Zumar with His words: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed, and the prophets and witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be passed between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.﴾

Allah's words:

﴿For every nation there is a term. When their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah states explicitly that for every nation there is a term (ajal), and that no one can go ahead of his specified term, nor can he be delayed beyond it.

He clarifies this meaning in many verses, such as:

• His words: ﴿No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay﴾ ([al-Hijr: 5 - 23 \ 43]),

• His words: ﴿Indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, is not deferred, if only you knew﴾ (Nuh: 4),

• His words: ﴿And Allah will never delay a soul when its term has come﴾ (al-Munafiqun: 11),

along with other verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is it [only] now, when it has befallen you, that you believe in it, while you were [previously] seeking to hasten it?﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that the disbelievers, out of disbelief and obstinacy, seek to hasten the punishment in this world. When they witness the punishment, they believe, but that belief at the moment of witnessing the punishment and its presence is not accepted from them. Allah has rebuked them for this here by saying: ﴿Is it [only] when it has befallen you that you believe in it?﴾ [Yunus: 51]. He also negated the acceptance of their faith at that time by saying: ﴿Is it [only] now, when you were previously seeking to hasten it?﴾.

This meaning is clarified in other verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿So when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ ﴿But their faith was not going to benefit them when they saw Our punishment. [This is] the established way of Allah which has passed on His servants. And the disbelievers were lost therein.﴾ [Ghafir: 84, 85],

• And His saying: ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims."﴾ ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were of the corrupters.﴾ [Yunus: 90, 91],

• And His saying: ﴿And repentance is not [accepted] from those who continue to do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now."﴾ [An-Nisa': 18], the verse [continues],

and other verses to this effect.

Allah, exalted is He, made an exception of the people of Yunus (ʿAlayhi as-salam, Jonah) alone, by His saying: ﴿Had there been a town that believed and its faith benefited it, [it would have been like] the people of Yunus. When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and let them enjoy for a time.﴾ [Yunus: 98].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 81:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah will surely nullify it﴾, and the rest of the verse.

He, may He be exalted, mentions about Musa in this verse that he said: Indeed, Allah will nullify the magic of Pharaoh's magicians.

In other places He explicitly states that what Musa said would happen, namely Allah's nullification of their magic, has in fact occurred. As in His saying: ﴿So the truth was established and what they were doing was nullified﴾ and ﴿So they were overcome there and turned back humbled﴾ [al-A'raf: 118, 119], and similar verses.

The author said in (*Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab*):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, You have indeed given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world. Our Lord, that they may lead [people] astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.﴾

In this verse, God explicitly states that this is the supplication of Musa, and He did not mention anyone with him. Then He said: ﴿Your supplication has been answered, so remain steadfast.﴾

The answer is that when Musa supplicated, Harun said "amin" (*ta'min*, saying "Amen") to his supplication, and the one who says "amin" (*al-mu'ammin*) is one of those who supplicate. This collective attribution is narrated from Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Salih, 'Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas. This is what Ibn Kathir said. From this verse, some scholars derived the ruling that the recitation (*qira'ah*) of the imam suffices for the follower (*ma'mum*, one who prays behind an imam) if the follower says "amin" to his recitation, because his saying "amin" is equivalent to his reciting.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 93:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly settled the Children of Israel in a good dwelling-place⁠﴾ — the verse.

He, exalted is He, mentions in this verse that He settled the Children of Israel in a dwelling-place of truthfulness (mubawwa' sidq).

And He explained this in other verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land, which We had blessed⁠﴾ — the verse [al-A'raf: 137],

• and His saying: ﴿And We removed them from gardens and springs﴾ ﴿and treasures and a noble station⁠﴾ [al-Dukhan: 25, 26] up to His saying: ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them⁠﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 59],

• and His saying: ﴿How many gardens and springs did they leave behind﴾ ﴿and crops and a noble station⁠﴾ [al-Dukhan: 25, 26] up to His saying: ﴿Thus, and We caused another people to inherit them⁠﴾ [al-Dukhan: 28].

The meaning of ﴿We certainly settled the Children of Israel in a good dwelling-place⁠﴾ is: We caused them to dwell in a pleasing and good place.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 96:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe﴾ ﴿Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, explicitly states that the one upon whom the word of punishment (al-'adhab) has been justified, and for whom wretchedness (al-shaqawa) has preceded in the knowledge of Allah, the clarity of the proofs of the truth will not benefit him. He mentioned this meaning in many verses,

• such as His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus: 101],

• and His statement: ﴿And even if they see a sign, they turn away﴾ [al-Qamar: 2],

• and His statement: ﴿And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it﴾ [al-An'am: 4],

• and His statement: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾ [Yusuf: 105],

• and His statement: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [al-Baqara: 6].

The verses with the like of this are very numerous.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 98:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except the people of Yunus; when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and We let them enjoy for a time.﴾

The apparent meaning of this noble verse is that the faith of the people of Yunus (Yunus: the Prophet Jonah) benefited them only in this world and not in the Hereafter, because of His saying: ﴿We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world.﴾

And it is understood, by the implication of the opposite (mafhum al-mukhalafa, the reasoning by contrary implication) in His saying: ﴿in the life of this world⦆, that the Hereafter is not like that. However, He, exalted is He, applied to them the name of belief without any restriction in Surat al-Saffat, and belief rescues from the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. Just as He also clarified in al-Saffat their great number, and all of that is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more.﴾ ﴿So they believed, and We let them enjoy for a time.﴾ [al-Saffat: 147, 148].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 99:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them, entirely﴾ — the verse.

In this noble verse, exalted is He declares explicitly that if He had willed the faith of all the people of the earth, they would all have believed, entirely. This is a clear proof that their disbelief occurs by His will that is universal and decreed (al-mashi'a al-kawniyya al-qadariyya), and He has explained this also in many verses:

• such as His saying: ﴿And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated[, i.e., set up partners]﴾ — the verse [al-An'am: 107],

• and His saying: ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾ [al-Sajda: 13],

• and His saying: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have brought them together upon guidance﴾ [al-An'am: 107],

and other verses besides these.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then would you compel the people until they become believers?﴾

In this noble verse, exalted is He has made clear that whoever Allah does not guide has no guide, and no one can compel his heart to open up (al-inshirah) to faith unless Allah wills that for him.

He has clarified this meaning in many verses:

• such as His saying: ﴿And whoever Allah intends for trial, you will not possess for him anything from Allah﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 41],

• and His saying: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide those who misguide [whom He leaves astray]﴾ — the verse [al-Nahl: 37] (p-163),

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ — the verse [al-Qasas: 56],

• and His saying: ﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him﴾ [al-A'raf: 186],

and verses of this kind are very numerous, as has preceded in "al-Nisa'".

The apparent view is that it is not abrogated (mansukha), and that its meaning is that none guides the hearts and directs them to good except Allah, exalted is He. The clearest evidence for this is that Allah followed it with His saying: ﴿And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah﴾ — the verse [Yunus: 100].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 101:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ — the verse.

Allah, exalted and majestic is He, commanded all His servants to look at what He created in the heavens and the earth of creatures that point to the greatness of their Creator, His perfection, His majesty, and His worthiness to be worshipped alone, exalted is He.

He alluded to something similar in His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53] — the verse. In Surah al-A'raf He rebuked the one who did not comply with this command and warned him that death may come upon him suddenly, so that his term ends before he looks into what Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to look into. Thereby He draws attention to the obligation of hastening to comply with the command of Allah, exalted is He. This is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and what things Allah has created, and that perhaps their term has drawn near?﴾ [al-A'raf: 185] — the verse.

Caution

This verse of al-A'raf that we have mentioned clearly indicates that a command necessitates immediacy (al-fawr, "immediate performance"), which is the position of the majority of the usuliyyun (scholars of the principles of jurisprudence), in contrast to a group of the Shafi'is and others.

Allah's statement: ﴿And that you should set your face toward the religion⁠﴾.

He clarified this meaning in His statement: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the natural disposition (fitrah) of Allah upon which He created mankind⁠﴾.

The words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿And do not call upon other than Allah that which can neither benefit you nor harm you﴾.

He also clarified its meaning with His words: ﴿And do not call upon another god besides Allah. There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face. To Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned﴾.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 109:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And be patient until Allah judges, and He is the best of judges﴾.

Here He did not specify what Allah judged between His Prophet and his enemies. But He has made it clear in many verses that He judged by giving him victory over them and making His religion manifest over every (p-164) religion,

• such as His saying: ﴿When the help of Allah comes and the victory﴾ [an-Nasr: 1] to the end of the surah,

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory﴾ [al-Fath: 1] to its end,

• and His saying: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts? And Allah judges; there is no repeller of His judgment﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 41], the verse.

And other verses besides these.
